targets.title: Logic feels so good—I like it! Evidence for intuitive detection of logicality in syllogistic reasoning.
targets.evidence_quote:
The present Experiments 1a, 1b, and 1c implemented replica-

tions of the intuitive condition of MH’s Experiment 4 in which

liking ratings for the syllogisms’ conclusions were obtained.
targets.outcome_quote: In a series of 6 experiments, we replicated effects of logical status on liking ratings of difficult syllogisms (although their shape differs from that reported by Morsanyi and Handley), and we tested 2 alternative accounts of our and Morsanyi and Handley's findings in terms of surface features accidentally confounded with logical status: the partial-repetition hypothesis and the content-effects hypothesis. The results support the content-effects hypothesis, according to which the effects of logical status reflect differences in mean liking for the presented conclusions rather than effects of logical status itself.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors obtain logical-status effects using the original materials but demonstrate that content confounds explain these effects. This methodological critique is the main message; controlling content eliminates the effect.

reasoning: New samples test Morsanyi and Handley, primarily their Experiment 4. One original paper is targeted. Other references provide theory, analytical methods or future applications. Title, DOI and both authors match. The ResearchGate page labels a preview but the extracted document spans all nine pages 1265–1273, includes six experiments, general discussion and complete references; this is full text.
